note: Phase 10B Section 5: storage theory extended to Q5_0/Q5_1, from ggml's real block formats (ggml-common.h, pinned llama.cpp commit c0bc8591). Q4_0/Q8_0/F16 repeated from Phase 10A for one complete table.

Q8_0.struct_layout: ggml_half d (2 bytes scale) + int8_t qs[32]

Q5_1.struct_layout: ggml_half d + ggml_half m (4 bytes scale+min) + uint8_t qh[4] (5th quant bit) + uint8_t qs[16] (4 low bits)

Q5_0.struct_layout: ggml_half d (2 bytes scale, no min) + uint8_t qh[4] (5th quant bit) + uint8_t qs[16] (4 low bits)

Q4_0.struct_layout: ggml_half d (2 bytes scale, no min) + uint8_t qs[16] (packed nibbles)

monotonic_ordering_bytes: Q4_0 < Q5_0 < Q5_1 < Q8_0 < F16 -- confirmed by both struct math and every observed allocation in this phase.

observed_vs_expected_at_ctx512_135m.consistency: EXACT MATCH to expected ratios (34.375%/37.5%) -- no discrepancy.

explicit_caveat: Q5_0 (5.5 bits/element) is 22 bytes/block, not simply '5 bits = 5/16'; the extra 0.5 bits/element comes from the qh[] 5th-bit-per-quant group, same overhead-beyond-nominal-bit-width pattern as Q4_0's 4.5 vs nominal 4. Q5_1 additionally carries a per-block min (like Q4_1 vs Q4_0), costing one more ggml_half (2 bytes/32 elements = 0.5 bits/element) than Q5_0.
